visuals.title: Where it starts and spreads
visuals.text: Arises in the peripheral zone of the prostate and spreads mainly to bone, especially the spine.

visuals.title: The diagnostic pathway
nodes: Raised PSA or hard, irregular DRE

visual.label: Example 12
visual.caption: Normal is below 4 ng/mL; avoid testing within 48 h of ejaculation or vigorous exercise, or with UTI.
Two patterns each scored out of 5 and added; the first number is the most common pattern.

visuals.title: Suspected cord compression
nodes: Back pain, leg weakness, new incontinence

events.x: Anti-androgen (flutamide or cyproterone) given at start

glossary.Malignant: Cancerous: able to invade nearby tissue and spread.
glossary.Central zone: The part of the prostate surrounding the ejaculatory ducts; rarely the site of cancer.
glossary.Afro-Caribbean: Of African or Caribbean descent, the highest-risk group for prostate cancer.
glossary.Asymmetric: Uneven, with one side different from the other.
glossary.Instrumentation: Passing instruments such as a catheter or cystoscope into the urinary tract.
glossary.Acute urinary retention: Sudden, painful inability to pass urine.
glossary.Metastases: Secondary tumours that have spread from the original cancer.
glossary.Bone metastases: Cancer deposits that have spread to bone.
glossary.Limb weakness: Reduced power in the arms or legs.
glossary.Sensory loss: Reduced feeling such as numbness in part of the body.
glossary.Lumbar vertebrae: The five bones of the lower back.
glossary.Pathological fracture: A break through bone weakened by disease, often after minimal trauma.
glossary.Biopsy: Removing a small sample of tissue to examine under a microscope.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease.
glossary.Gleason X: Gleason score that cannot be determined from the sample.
glossary.Ejaculation: Release of semen, which can temporarily raise PSA.
glossary.Prostatitis: Inflammation or infection of the prostate.
glossary.NICE: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, which sets UK clinical guidelines.
glossary.Staging: Working out how far a cancer has spread.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.Serum creatinine: A blood marker of kidney function; it rises when the kidneys fail.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function.
glossary.Localised: Confined to the organ where it started.
glossary.Life expectancy: How long a person is expected to live.
glossary.Comorbidities: Other medical conditions a patient has alongside the main one.
glossary.Stage T2c: Tumour involving both lobes of the prostate but still inside the gland.
glossary.T2N0M0: Tumour confined to the prostate, with no node spread and no distant metastases.
glossary.Erectile dysfunction: Inability to achieve or keep an erection.
glossary.Radiotherapy: Treatment that uses ionising radiation to kill cancer cells.
glossary.Androgen: Male sex hormone such as testosterone, which drives prostate cancer growth.
glossary.Surgical decompression: An operation to relieve pressure on the spinal cord.
glossary.Serine protease: An enzyme that cuts proteins; PSA is one, made by prostate cells.
glossary.Glandular architecture: The normal arrangement of glands within a tissue.
glossary.Infiltrative: Growing into and through surrounding tissue.
glossary.Pituitary: Gland at the base of the brain that releases LH, which drives testosterone production.
glossary.Downregulate: To reduce the number or response of receptors after continuous stimulation.
glossary.Testosterone surge: A temporary rise in testosterone when a GnRH agonist is first started.
glossary.MRI spine: Magnetic resonance scan of the spine, the gold standard for suspected cord compression.
